newsitem.title: USA: Hartford arena seen surviving without NHL team.
newsitem.headline: Hartford arena seen surviving without NHL team.

text.p: The departure of the National Hockey League Hartford Whalers is not necessarily a fatal blow for the Hartford Civic Center, city planners and entertainment officials were quoted as saying on Tuesday.
The Hartford Courant reported that an expected strong mix of entertainment and sports events could keep the 22-year-old Civic Center busy, and help the local economy.
The Whalers, Connecticut's only major league sports franchise, left Hartford earlier this year in favor of North Carolina.
The NHL team pumped about $73 million a year into Hartford's economy, recent studies had shown.
The Civic Center, owned by Connecticut Development Authority, will now try to survive on college and more minor professional sports.

Events will include University of Connecticut men's and women's basketball, the New England Blizzard of the American Basketball League, the Connecticut Pride of the Continental Basketball League, and most likely a new American Hockey League or International Hockey League franchise.
The Blizzard will probably attract about 12,000 spectators per game, the report projected.
"That's going to put a lot of money into the Hartford Civic Center's pocket, no question about it," said Kevin Barrett, general manager of the Springfield Civic Center.
"Yes, they lost a major league tenant, but they can replace it with good stuff."
The Civic Center coliseum expects to host about 182 events this year, up from 170 last year.
But the adjoining Civic Center Mall is still a problem and has lost $56 million since its opening in 1975, the report said.
